devon: Heads-up — hitting weirdness converting HF Jinja chat_template -> Redwood prompt for the new onboard (meta-7b-qat). System message sometimes gets dropped and raw tokens like  show up in completions. Example template below, any ideas?

devon: ```
{% raw %}{% set user_name = user.name or "User" %}
<|system|>
You are a helpful assistant that answers succinctly.
<|endoftext|>
<|user|>
{{ user_name }}: {{ instruction }}
<|assistant|>
{% endraw %}```

maria: Two common issues here: (1) special tokens vs role markers — HF model authors sometimes use explicit special tokens (<|system|>) that aren't in the tokenizer, so they become literal text; (2) Jinja conditionals/macros can produce empty blocks that our converter treats as no-op and drops the system role.

alex: Also check model config.json/tokenizer.json — is there an eos_token or additional_special_tokens entry? If not, HF will inline them. We saw  appear when eos/special tokens mismatched during generation.

sasha: I reproduced a quality regression after INT8 QAT: when the system prefix is lost, the model drifts on role following. Eval diffs: ~4% BLEU drop on instruction-following, reply_accuracy down ~6% on our chat eval set. So it's not just cosmetic.

devon: Proposed conversion steps: parse Jinja into ordered role blocks, map HF role markers to Redwood role prefixes, and normalize special tokens. Example mapping:

- `<|system|>` -> `<<SYSTEM>>` (or Redwood structured system message)
- `<|user|>` -> `<<USER>>`
- `<|assistant|>` -> `<<ASSISTANT>>`

Also: if tokenizer supports the special token (present in tokenizer.json), preserve it; otherwise strip it and insert human-readable role markers so the model still sees the role context.

raman: I'll add a unit test to the onboarding harness: re-render N templates with canonical inputs and assert token sequences before/after conversion are semantically equivalent (modulo added role markers). Also will schedule a quantized-vs-fp16 eval with fixed seeds to catch regressions. I'll own this, ETA EOW.

maria: Small pseudo convert helper I used locally:```
# pseudo-code
def convert_jinja_to_redwood(template, tokenizer):
    blocks = parse_jinja_blocks(template)  # yields (role, text) in order
    out = []
    for role, body in blocks:
        text = strip_unknown_special_tokens(body, tokenizer)
        if role == 'system':
            out.append('<<SYSTEM>> ' + text)
        elif role == 'user':
            out.append('<<USER>> ' + text)
        elif role == 'assistant':
            out.append('<<ASSISTANT>> ' + text)
    return '\n'.join(out)
```

alex: Practical checks to add: assert any(s in tokenizer.get("additional_special_tokens", []) for s in ["<|system|>", "<|assistant|>"]) else warn. Also log token ids when conversion happens so we can diff.
